extracted.intended_audience: neuroscience researchers, science educators, and NIH SBIR-interested readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative criteria and concerns relevant to a small-business NIH SBIR proposal to produce classroom neuroscience kits (SpikerBox/RoboRoach), including technical, educational, ethical, legal, and public-impact dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device characteristics: easy-to-use, inexpensive, portable, and functional
rubrics_metrics.description: The SpikerBox is described as a bio-amplifier that is easy-to-use, inexpensive (<$100), portable, and can detect and record the spiking activity (action potentials) of invertebrates such as crickets and cockroaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a funded product, the device should be low-cost (<$100), user-friendly for secondary school students, portable for classroom use, and technically capable of reliably detecting/recording neural spikes from target invertebrates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete classroom-ready educational materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim: To develop the full lesson materials including curricula, lesson plans, lab books, and assessments to allow our SpikerBox to be used in classrooms as an enabling tool to teach neuroscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding/implementation should include comprehensive teaching materials (curriculum, lesson plans, lab manuals, and assessment instruments) so teachers can deploy the kit without requiring specialized lab infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying data analysis software usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim: To develop easy-to-use data analysis software to accompany the SpikerBox and allow basic neural analysis routines on an iPad or standard laptop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software must be intuitive for school-aged users, run on common consumer hardware (iPad/laptop), and include basic neural-analysis routines appropriate for the educational level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on demonstration kit (RoboRoach) for concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim: To develop prototypes of the 'RoboRoach,' a kit modified from off-the-shelf remote control toys that mounts on a cockroach, delivers pulses to the antennae nerves, and allows remote control of cockroach locomotion—useful for teaching microstimulation, electronics, and behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kits demonstrating microstimulation and neural control should be designed to illustrate concepts safely and clearly; prototypes must balance demonstrability with animal welfare and classroom practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable educational outcomes (understanding and retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: By allowing secondary school students to do real electrophysiology experiments in the classroom, we will increase understanding and retention of neuroscience concepts at an early age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include plans to measure educational impact (e.g., retention, conceptual understanding) empirically—ideally via formal studies—to support claims of improved learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health relevance / workforce pipeline justification
rubrics_metrics.description: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE: Backyard Brains will develop a 'SpikerBox' kit ... By allowing these students to do what was previously only available in advanced college, we aim to inspire the next generation of scientists, physicians, and engineers, as well as accelerate fundamental neuroscience research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should articulate how the educational product contributes to public health (e.g., by inspiring future scientists, improving STEM performance, or accelerating research that could lead to therapies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations of animal use
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple commenters argue there are ethical issues even if no legal restrictions exist: the presence of neurocircuitry raises questions about feeling/pain; animal use should be limited and taught alongside ethics (e.g., the three R's).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for invertebrates, proposals should address ethical concerns: include education on animal-use ethics, justify animal procedures, minimize harm, and consider student emotional responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/compliance with jurisdictional animal-use rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters note: 'There are no legal requirements in relation to doing experiments on cockroaches and crickets' (US context), but elsewhere (many European countries) laws restrict invasive experiments in schools and IACUC distinctions vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must ensure compliance with local, regional, and national laws/regulations concerning animal experiments in educational settings and be explicit about differing international legal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of simulation/alternatives when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative view: well-made simulation software (eg. Sniffy The Virtual Rat) can deliver educational objectives without animals; simulations avoid uncontrolled data and ethical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether learning objectives can be met by virtual models; if so, prioritize alternatives to live-animal use or include them as options to accommodate ethical objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity and necessity of live-animal experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that live-animal experiments in classroom settings may not provide novel outcomes and that their scientific/educational gain over simulations is disputable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear justification that live-animal exercises provide unique pedagogical or scientific value that cannot be achieved through simulations or demonstrations; avoid gratuitous vivisection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal welfare minimization practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Backyard Brains reply: cockroaches tolerate 1-2 missing legs; nymphs regrow legs; cockroaches are not killed, backpacks used briefly, and animals 'retire' after experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe specific welfare measures (non-lethal protocols, short exposure times, post-experiment care/retirement) to minimize animal suffering and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of public perception and PR risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments warn of potential political backlash (e.g., critique that taxpayer money used to 'teach Jr high and high school students how to record electricity from cockroaches') and PR concerns about projects like 'RoboRoach.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should anticipate and mitigate public and political criticism—prepare communication plans, emphasize ethical safeguards and educational benefits, and consider audience sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal assessment plan embedded in the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Backyard Brains: 'One the aims of this grant is determine if our experiments in a classroom improve retention of neuroscience concepts. Operationally, the answer is “Of Course!” as kids are often blown away ... but as scientists we are doing the formal study to show this.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a rigorous, pre-specified evaluation methodology (control/comparison groups, validated assessments) to demonstrate claimed educational outcomes rather than relying on anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratization and lowering barriers to science
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents argue bringing neurotechnology into high schools lowers barriers to entry, fosters curiosity, and accelerates innovation (analogy: astronomy access versus neuroscience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider equity and access—design products and dissemination plans that enable broad participation beyond elite institutions to support STEM pipeline goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to real-world neuroscience/clinical applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Backyard Brains links classroom microstimulation demos to technologies used in treating Parkinson’s disease, depression, and deafness, arguing pedagogical relevance to real clinical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground educational demonstrations in connections to real-world research/clinical applications where appropriate, but avoid overstating translational impact; justify claims with concrete examples.
